extra.message: The csrf_image view is decorated with @csrf_exempt, disabling Django's CSRF protection for this endpoint. This allows cross-site request forgery attacks where an attacker can trick authenticated users into making unintended requests to this view.

The CSRF middleware 'django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware' is commented out in MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES, disabling CSRF protection globally for all views by default. This leaves the entire application vulnerable to cross-site request forgery attacks.

The Django SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in the settings file as 'h++jszpm)i@p%ay_b=cp#()^od!qns14)h%@qm3)p=cuo+st^a'. This key is used for cryptographic signing of sessions and CSRF tokens. If leaked (e.g., via the path traversal vulnerability in user_pic), an attacker can forge sessions and CSRF tokens.

DEBUG = True is enabled in settings. In production, this exposes detailed error pages with stack traces, local variables, and settings values (including SECRET_KEY), leaking sensitive information to attackers. Combined with the boom view that deliberately raises exceptions, this creates an information disclosure risk.

The show_toolbar callback enables the Django Debug Toolbar when any request contains a 'debug' parameter in GET, POST, or cookies. This allows any user to activate the debug toolbar by adding ?debug=1 to any URL, exposing sensitive application internals including SQL queries, settings, and request/response data.
